primitives.name: Calibrated Confidence Tier
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Calibrated confidence tier** — a top tier where a pick labeled ~70% *actually wins ~70%* of the time, measured over a real settled sample and shown as a reliability curve.
primitives.assumptions: Confidence labels are generated by a well-calibrated model; outcomes are binary (win/loss); reliability is assessed over a large enough sample size.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When p < 0.5 or p > 0.9, calibration drift exceeds threshold (Brier > 0.05), triggering re-evaluation.

layer2.mapping: GSI's calibrated probability estimates mirror GSE's confidence state transitions through reliability curves and Brier score thresholds.
layer2.telemetry: Reliability curve slope, Brier score, ECE (Expected Calibration Error)

primitives.verbatim_quote: > The model-changing steps below are **founder-gated `MODEL_VERSION` decisions** — this document > sequences them; it does not flip them.
primitives.assumptions: Only authorized personnel can increment MV; changes are tested before activation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If MV is incremented without human approval, system halts until manual override.

layer2.mapping: GSE's state transition logic depends on GSI's calibrated signal integrity, which is enforced via founder-gated MV updates.

primitives.name: Edge Significance Test
primitives.verbatim_quote: Win rate is a function of **what you choose to grade**.
primitives.assumptions: Edge is statistically significant if p_value < 0.05 and n > 100.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If p_value ≥ 0.05, edge is considered noise and not used for confidence adjustment.

layer2.telemetry: p_value distribution, sample size per edge type

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that a 70% win rate is not an absolute claim but a calibrated reliability measure. It requires a dual approach: first, generating predictions with isotonic calibration (PAVA) to ensure label accuracy; second, validating these labels against actual outcomes using Brier score and Expected Calibration Error (ECE). The system avoids fabricating blended win rates by enforcing strict data filtering—only non-bootstrap, canonical, learning-eligible picks are included. Each MODEL_VERSION update is gated by human oversight, ensuring that changes are not autonomous but deliberate. The process also includes continuous drift monitoring, where if Brier delta exceeds 0.05, the system suspends operations until recalibration occurs. This creates a feedback loop of improvement and accountability, forming a robust foundation for trust in performance claims.
